mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES mobility is a leading indicator of more weekday trips, which then spill into nearby retail visits and lift RETAIL_REC over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -36.9 to -30.4 while RETAIL_REC improved from -41.7 to -37.6 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps rising for the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM becomes less negative, households shift from online substitution back to in-person errands, and this same errand rebound raises RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -10 and stays there for 2 weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -17.7 to -9.9 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -10 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES increases access to shopping districts and commuting-related foot traffic, producing a stronger rise in RETAIL_REC than either series alone.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both became less negative over the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve over the next month but RETAIL_REC does not rise more than its prior four-week average, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals more time spent outside the home, which should translate into higher discretionary retail visits and a higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 12.4 to 10.6 while RETAIL_REC improved from -41.3 to -37.6
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls further but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the last four weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in PARKS mobility indicates relaxed activity constraints and broader social mixing, which should spill into shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC after a short lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a sub -60 level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -65.0 to -59.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS jumps by at least 5 points from below -60 and RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week, this signal is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-mobility holiday-shopping regime, rising GROCERY_PHARM combined with rising TRANSIT captures errand bundling and mall access, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT improved steadily across the four weekly means
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT keep improving together but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-four-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues to recover to within 30 points below baseline, the easing is large enough to reopen access to retail corridors and lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -30 and stays there for 2 weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -29.6 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved to -37.6
failure_condition: If TRANSIT moves above -30 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES rises, the same people are spending less time at home and more time in commuting and destination activity, which should increase retail visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined while WORKPLACES rebounded in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL keeps falling and WORKPLACES keeps rising but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the previous four weeks, the mechanism is falsified.
